DE over time course

Source: R/DE_timecourse.R
DE_timecourse.Rd

Differential expression analysis of temporal changes within and between groups by limma, using time as a factor or a numeric variable for linear or spline models.

Usage

DE_timecourse(
  se_obj,
  group = NULL,
  reference_group = NULL,
  assay,
  group_mode = c("per_group", "joint_group"),
  time_mode = c("factor", "numeric", "spline"),
  spline_df = 3,
  trend = FALSE,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH"
)

Arguments

se_obj

A SummarizedExperiment object created by create_input().

group

A character vector specifying which groups to analyse. If NULL, all groups in the Group column are used.

reference_group

A single reference group for a joint_group model. If NULL, the first group in group or colData(se_obj)$Group is used and reported by a message.

assay

The assay to use in the SummarizedExperiment object: a numeric index or character name, e.g. 1 or "orig" for original data, 2 or "norm" for time 0 normalised data. The selected assay should contain log-transformed, normalised values. A warning is issued if the data appears to be un-logged raw counts.

group_mode

"per_group" or "joint_group".

  • "per_group" tests each group separately.

  • "joint_group" fits one group-by-time model across the selected groups.

time_mode

"factor", "numeric", or "spline".

  • "factor" treats time as a categorical variable. The earliest available time point is the reference, and each later time point is compared with it. All temporal terms are tested jointly with an omnibus F-test. With one temporal term, this is equivalent to a two-sided t-test.

  • "numeric" treats time as continuous and tests one linear trend.

  • "spline" models time with a natural cubic spline basis, allowing a smooth non-linear trajectory. The spline coefficients are tested jointly with an omnibus F-test.

spline_df

An integer of degrees of freedom when time_mode = "spline", controlling the flexibility of the fitted trajectory. Larger values allow more complex trajectories but may increase overfitting. It must be at least 2 and smaller than the number of time points used by the model. Default: 3.

trend

Logical, passed to limma::eBayes(). Use TRUE only when the mean-variance relationship is expected to vary with abundance. The default FALSE is usually appropriate for log-transformed, normalised data unless diagnostics support modelling a mean-variance trend.

pAdjustMethod

P-value adjustment method passed to stats::p.adjust() for the returned result tables. Must be one of stats::p.adjust.methods. Default: "BH".

Value

A list with results, fits, design, and metadata.

In a per_group model, results contains a table named time_effect.

In a joint_group model, results contains tables named reference_time_effect, global_time_effect, group_effect, global_group_effect, and group_time_interaction.

Result tables report an omnibus F statistic, P.Value, and adj.P.Val. For a table testing a single model term, F = t^2.

Columns in results tables have effect-specific names. For time effect tables,

  • time_mode = "factor" uses logFC_TimeFactor<time> (log-scale changes relative to the reference time)

  • time_mode = "numeric" uses logFC_TimeSlope (log-scale changes per time unit)

  • time_mode = "spline" uses SplineBasis_1, SplineBasis_2, etc.

In joint_group results, group-by-time differences use names such as

  • time_mode = "factor": delta_logFC_GroupX_TimeFactor<time>

  • time_mode = "numeric": delta_logFC_GroupX_TimeSlope

  • time_mode = "spline": delta_SplineBasis_GroupX_1, etc.

The global_group_effect table reports group main-effect model coefficients as GroupX (X is a non-reference group), alongside group-by-time terms; group_effect table reports each non-reference group's estimated difference from the reference group at the reference time (ReferenceTime) by columns of logFC_GroupX_at_reference_time.

These names apply only to results table columns; fits and design retain the original model coefficient names.

Features with missing values are fitted using their available observations when the model remains estimable. Features with insufficient observations or non-estimable designs return in the results with NA for model coefficients, test statistics, and p-values.

Details

If colData(se_obj) contains Subject, repeated measurements are modelled with limma::duplicateCorrelation().

Missingness patterns are defined by whether each Group-Time combination contains at least one finite value.

The joint model is fit on the shared time points and shared features of all selected groups. Excluded or non-estimable features are retained in the results with NA.

Multiple testing correction is applied within each group for per_group results and separately within each joint_group result table, after combining all missingness patterns.

ReferenceTime is the earliest time point available in each fitting pattern and is used for group_effect in all time modes and for temporal comparisons in factor mode. It is NA for numeric and spline temporal tests.

In a joint model,

  • reference_time_effect tests whether the reference group changes over time

  • group_time_interaction tests whether the other groups have different temporal patterns

  • global_time_effect tests all time and group-by-time terms jointly, asking whether any selected group has a temporal effect

  • group_effect tests selected group differences at the earliest (reference) time point used by each missingness pattern

  • global_group_effect tests all group and group-by-time terms jointly, asking whether group trajectories differ anywhere in the fitted time course.

Examples

data(example_obj)

per_group_result <- DE_timecourse(
    example_obj, assay = 2, group_mode = "per_group"
)
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
#> Some Group-Time combinations contain only one sample; replicate-level variance cannot be estimated for them.
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
#> Some Group-Time combinations contain only one sample; replicate-level variance cannot be estimated for them.
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
joint_result <- DE_timecourse(
    example_obj, assay = 2,
    group = c("IFNbeta", "IFNgamma"),
    group_mode = "joint_group", reference_group = "IFNgamma"
)
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
